common_name: Samuel Sommer Southern Magnolia (Giant-Flowered Southern Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil, giving Samuel Sommer generous room since it grows into one of the largest-leaved, largest-flowered selections of Southern magnolia.

directions: Samuel Sommer is prized for having some of the largest flowers and leaves of any Southern magnolia cultivar, with blossoms that can exceed a foot across and glossy, deep-green leaves carrying a light rusty indumentum underneath. It grows into a dense, broadly pyramidal specimen tree best suited to expansive properties where its ultimate size will not overwhelm the setting. Give it deep, well-drained soil and consistent moisture while establishing, then expect a vigorous grower that tolerates Gulf Coast heat and humidity with ease. It is somewhat less cold-hardy than selections like Edith Bogue or Bracken's Brown Beauty, so it performs best in zone 8 and warmer.

common_name: St. Mary Southern Magnolia (Compact Early-Blooming Southern Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; St. Mary's compact, shrubby habit suits it to smaller residential lots where a full-size Southern magnolia would be too large.

directions: St. Mary is a compact, densely branched Southern magnolia selection that begins flowering at a younger age than the straight species, producing abundant fragrant white blooms even on relatively small trees. Its naturally shrubby, multi-stemmed habit makes it useful as a large screening shrub or small specimen tree without the extensive pruning needed to keep a seedling-grown magnolia in bounds. The dark green foliage carries light bronze felting underneath, giving some seasonal interest when the wind lifts the leaves. It adapts well to the humid, heavy soils common along the Gulf Coast and tolerates both heat and brief cold snaps once established.

common_name: Greenback Southern Magnolia (Compact Fine-Textured Southern Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Greenback's smaller leaves and denser branching give it a finer texture than standard Southern magnolia in tighter landscape spaces.

directions: Greenback stands out among Southern magnolia cultivars for its noticeably smaller, narrower leaves and dense, tidy branching, giving mature trees a finer-textured, more refined silhouette than the coarse-leaved species type. It still produces the classic large, fragrant white flowers in late spring and summer, but on a plant that reads less bulky in the landscape. This selection tolerates the heat, humidity, and periodic heavy rainfall typical of the Gulf Coast without difficulty, and its dense canopy makes an effective visual screen or specimen tree. Provide deep, well-drained soil and regular watering through the first two years to establish a strong root system.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or B&B trees in spring in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Russet's heavy rust-brown leaf indumentum is most vivid when the tree receives full sun exposure.

directions: Russet is grown chiefly for its thick, rust-colored indumentum coating the underside of its dark green leaves, an even heavier and more uniformly coppery covering than seen on selections like D.D. Blanchard, which shows especially well when planted where afternoon light passes through the canopy. It matures into a dense, pyramidal tree of substantial size, well suited to use as a specimen or screening tree on larger properties. Flowering is typical of the species — large, fragrant, creamy-white blooms from late spring into summer — followed by the cone-like fruiting structures with bright red seeds. It performs reliably in Gulf Coast heat and humidity and needs only routine watering during establishment.

common_name: Saratoga Gold Yaupon Holly (Yellow-Berried Yaupon Holly)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Saratoga Gold's bright yellow berries show best against its fine, dark evergreen foliage when sited where winter sun highlights the fruiting branches.

directions: Saratoga Gold is a female yaupon holly selection notable for its clear golden-yellow berries, a striking departure from the typical red fruit of the species, held in dense clusters along fine-textured, small-leaved branches through fall and winter. Like other yaupon hollies it is exceptionally tough, tolerating drought, poor sandy soil, salt spray, and the heat and humidity of Gulf Coast summers with minimal care once established. A nearby male yaupon within pollinating distance improves fruit set, since female hollies need pollination to produce their showy berry display. It takes well to shearing for hedges but also looks handsome left in its naturally upright, twiggy form as a specimen or screening shrub, and its berries persist into winter as a food source for songbirds.
